transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, hello. I suppose what brings me in today is that, for the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always puttering around. I'm always fixing something, arranging things in the house, or volunteering for just one more thing. Even at 87, I just... I have a really hard time sitting down and being still.
Do you also find it hard to keep your attention focused on one thing?

No, not really. I don't seem to have trouble with that. When I'm working on one of my projects around the house, I can focus on it just fine until it's finished. My mind doesn't really wander off... it's just that I have to be doing something active. It's the sitting still part that gets me, not the paying attention.
Has this need to stay busy been a lifelong part of your personality, or is it something new that started only in the past year?

Well, it's definitely not a new thing. It's really been that way my whole life. I remember getting scolded way back in grade school because I was always popping out of my seat. The teachers would get frustrated because I'd talk over my classmates, and they always said I was just... too lively. And that was long before I was even a teenager. So, yes, I've always been like this.
Has this way of being caused you problems in your life?

Well, yes, it does cause some issues. At the senior center, for instance, I've actually had to go up and apologize to people after our meetings. I guess I just get too wound up and talk over folks. One of my good friends even pulled me aside and suggested I take a smaller role at the sign-up table... she said my whole manner was just making things a bit tense for everyone. So, yes, it does get in the way.
Do you also have a history of being forgetful or losing track of everyday things, like misplacing items or missing appointments?

No, I wouldn't say that. I keep my calendar pretty straight, and I know where my things are. My memory is fine... I don't really have trouble with losing things or missing appointments. It's just the restlessness that's the problem.
When you were younger, did you often act without thinking first?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I was always moving around and talking a mile a minute, like I said, but I didn't really do reckless things out of the blue. I usually knew what I was doing... I just couldn't sit still while I did it. So, no, acting without thinking wasn't really something I struggled with.
Would you say this lifelong restlessness and need to stay busy has mainly affected how you get along with other people?

Well, yes, I suppose that is the main thing. I manage my house and my daily routine just fine on my own, so it doesn't really get in the way there. It really just comes down to... well, what I mentioned before. My fidgeting and talking just rubs people the wrong way sometimes. So, yes, I'd say it mostly just affects how I get along with others. I haven't really noticed it causing problems anywhere else.
